observations.question: Is cardiomegaly present, and if so, what is its severity?
observations.observation: The provided chest radiographs demonstrate the cardiac silhouette. Assessing cardiomegaly and its severity requires precise measurements (cardio-thoracic ratio) which are not possible with qualitative assessment of the images alone. However, the heart size appears within normal limits on the PA and lateral views. There is no obvious enlargement of the cardiac silhouette. The lateral view shows a normal cardiac contour. The AP view is less useful for assessing cardiomegaly due to magnification.
observations.limitations: A definitive assessment of cardiomegaly requires quantitative measurements (cardio-thoracic ratio) and comparison to prior imaging if available. The quality of the images and the lack of a standardized scale make precise measurement impossible. The AP view is not ideal for assessing cardiac size. Without clinical context and patient history, it is difficult to determine if the observed cardiac size is truly normal for this individual.
